original_claim: FMCSA granting ~200 ghost-address authorities/month; approval rate halved after April 2025 identity-verification rollout
refined_claim: FMCSA launched mandatory biometric identity verification (via IDEMIA) for all new motor carrier, broker, and freight forwarder applications on April 1, 2025, targeting a long-standing vulnerability in the Unified Registration System. Industry analytics firm CarrierOK initially reported a ~50% drop in the filed-to-published conversion rate (from a typical 60-65% down to ~30% in April 2025), though the firm subsequently acknowledged its methodology was flawed. The '~200 ghost-address authorities/month' figure as stated conflates two separate issues: Secretary Duffy's documented remark about '200 DOT numbers going to a P.O. Box' (referring to ghost-office/PPOB concentration at a single address, not a monthly grant rate), and a broader industry claim about fraudulent monthly approvals that has no traceable primary-source citation. The April 2025 rollout itself is confirmed by official FMCSA sources; the quantified before/after approval-rate drop and the '~200/month' grant figure remain unsupported by any government statistical release, OIG audit, Federal Register data, or Congressional testimony.

recommendation_for_canonical_draft: Split the original claim into two separate assertions with different confidence levels: (1) CONFIRMED (Tier 1 sources): 'FMCSA launched mandatory biometric identity verification (IDEMIA) for all new motor carrier registrations on April 1, 2025, as part of its Unified Registration System modernization to combat carrier registration fraud.' Cite fmcsa.dot.gov/registration/identity-verification and the Federal Register Motus notice. (2) MARK AS [ASSUMED-N] or DROP: The specific figures — '~200 ghost-address authorities/month' and 'approval rate halved' — lack primary-source grounding. The '200' figure misrepresents Secretary Duffy's statement (which referred to 200 DOT numbers at one P.O. Box, not 200 monthly fraudulent grants). The approval-rate-halved statistic comes from a single industry analytics firm (CarrierOK) that publicly retracted its methodology. If a quantified impact claim is needed, the most defensible language based on available evidence is: 'Industry tracking data suggested newly published authorities fell roughly 50% in April–May 2025, though official FMCSA statistics confirming this magnitude have not been publicly released.' Flag for attended fetch of the DOT press release and FMCSA fact sheet PDFs before publishing.
